metadata.title: Individual Email SSPP
metadata.remarks: System Security and Privacy Plan defining trust boundaries, data handling, and accountability for individual human email mailboxes.

import-profile.remarks: Institutional baseline covering security, privacy, identity, records, and acceptable use requirements.

system-characteristics.system-description: Institutional email service providing individual human mailboxes for staff, faculty, and students for day-to-day communication, collaboration, and official correspondence.

information-type.title: Email Message Content
information-type.description: Content of email messages sent or received by an individual mailbox, including headers, body text, and inline elements.

information-type.title: Email Metadata
information-type.description: Envelope, header, routing, timestamp, and authentication metadata associated with email messages.

information-type.title: Mailbox State
information-type.description: Mailbox folders, message status (read/unread), retention state, and user-controlled organization.

information-type.title: Authentication and Access Events
information-type.description: Records of authentication, access, delegation, and security-relevant mailbox activity.

props.name: depends-on-sspp
props.remarks: Individual Email Service inherits all platform trust, security, and resiliency guarantees from the Secure Email Platform SSPP.

props.name: usage-class
props.remarks: This SSPP applies only to human-operated individual email mailboxes.

props.name: prohibited-usage
props.remarks: Individual mailboxes MUST NOT be used for bulk messaging, automated notifications, application inboxing, or campaign delivery.

props.name: usage-intent
props.remarks: This service is intended for human-initiated, conversational email communication conducted by an individual mailbox owner.

props.name: volume-constraint
props.remarks: Individual mailboxes are not authorized for bulk, mass, or campaign-style messaging. High-volume outbound email must use the Email Campaign Platform.

props.name: automation-constraint
props.remarks: Individual mailboxes MUST NOT be used as application senders or automated notification sources.

props.name: implicit-authority-constraint
props.remarks: Email messages from individual mailboxes MUST NOT be treated as implicit approvals, authorizations, or system-of-record transactions.

props.name: escalation-requirement
props.remarks: When communication scope, frequency, or impact exceeds individual messaging norms, users MUST transition to an approved platform (campaign, collaboration relay, or notification gateway).

props.name: monitoring-requirement
props.remarks: All individual email activity is subject to institutional security monitoring, inspection, and investigation regardless of forwarding configuration.

props.name: forwarding-monitoring-constraint
props.remarks: Forwarding to external email destinations does not remove institutional monitoring, detection, quarantine, or investigative authority.

props.name: external-forwarding
props.remarks: External forwarding is permitted only for users with an active student role, subject to monitoring and security enforcement.

props.name: external-forwarding
props.remarks: External forwarding is prohibited for staff, faculty, librarians, and affiliates due to institutional accountability and identity assurance requirements.

props.name: external-correspondence-constraint
props.remarks: Once an institutional email address is established for an individual, official institutional correspondence including helpdesk support, administrative communication, and security-related interaction MUST occur only via the institutional email address. External email addresses cannot be validated for identity or authority and MUST NOT be used for official correspondence.

props.name: support-interaction-constraint
props.remarks: Helpdesk and support functions MUST NOT validate, act on, or continue official cases initiated or conducted exclusively via external email addresses once an institutional email address exists.

props.name: access-termination
props.remarks: Access to individual email terminates immediately upon employment or affiliation end unless a concurrent student role exists.

props.name: post-termination-retention
props.remarks: Mailbox contents are retained and disposed of in accordance with institutional retention policy following role termination.

props.name: student-access-termination
props.remarks: Student access to individual email terminates immediately upon academic termination and within 90 days of graduation unless a new non-student relationship is established.

props.name: student-role-transition
props.remarks: Continued email access beyond student eligibility requires an active, formally established non-student role.

props.name: email-protection-mode
props.remarks: Email protections MAY filter, block, quarantine, recall, or remove malicious or deceptive content both before and after delivery.

props.name: user-override-constraint
props.remarks: End users cannot override institutional email security actions including quarantine, recall, or removal of messages.

props.name: authority-scope
props.remarks: Email sent from an individual mailbox represents only the individual sender and MUST NOT be treated as institutional authorization unless validated through an approved workflow.

props.name: mailbox-reuse
props.remarks: Individual mailboxes MUST NOT be repurposed, reassigned, or recycled for new users.

props.name: credential-sharing
props.remarks: Credentials for individual email accounts MUST NOT be shared or embedded in scripts or tools.

props.name: delegation-constraint
props.remarks: All access delegation must be explicit, auditable, and time bounded; blanket or undocumented delegation is prohibited.

props.name: information-use-constraint
props.remarks: Individual email mailboxes are intended for communication and coordination, not as primary repositories for documents, records, or long-term data storage.

props.name: attachment-handling-intent
props.remarks: Email attachments are treated as transient delivery mechanisms and must be stored in approved repositories if they require ongoing retention or sharing.

props.name: retention-authority
props.remarks: Retention and disposition of individual email content are governed by institutional retention policy and legal obligations, not user preference.

props.name: deletion-semantics
props.remarks: User deletion of email messages does not constitute authoritative destruction and may not remove messages from institutional archives or legal holds.

props.name: long-term-storage-constraint
props.remarks: Users must not use individual email mailboxes as long-term storage for operational, academic, or administrative records.

props.name: repository-escalation
props.remarks: Content requiring ongoing access, collaboration, or archival must be moved to an approved document or records repository.

props.name: system-of-record-constraint
props.remarks: Individual email mailboxes must not be treated as authoritative systems of record.

props.name: disclosure-default
props.remarks: Individual email content is not disclosed to third parties by default and is protected from routine access or review.

props.name: disclosure-authority
props.remarks: Disclosure of individual email content occurs only under documented legal, regulatory, or institutional authority.

props.name: disclosure-bases
props.remarks: Permissible disclosure bases include lawful process, freedom-of-information requests, records obligations, or authorized security investigations.

props.name: disclosure-policy-reference
props.remarks: Email disclosure conditions, limitations, and procedures are governed by the authoritative institutional data and information disclosure policy.

props.name: user-privacy-expectation
props.remarks: Users should not expect absolute confidentiality of individual email where lawful or policy-mandated disclosure applies.

props.name: disclosure-auditability
props.remarks: All access and disclosures of individual email content must be logged, reviewable, and attributable.

props.name: data-classification-constraint
props.remarks: Individual email mailboxes MUST NOT be used to transmit, store, or process information classified at Level 4 or higher.

props.name: classification-exception
props.remarks: Individual email MUST NOT be used to temporarily transmit or stage higher-classification data pending transfer to an approved system.

props.name: classification-escalation
props.remarks: Information classified at Level 4 or higher MUST be handled using approved secure storage, file transfer, or managed collaboration platforms.

props.name: discovery-constraint
props.remarks: Discovery of higher-classification information in email does not authorize its continued presence or use within individual mailboxes.

system-implementation.remarks: Individual Email Service trust is realized through explicit authority boundaries, authenticated identity, centralized platform enforcement, and retained audit evidence.

components.title: Individual Email Mailbox
components.description: Per-user mailbox enabling authenticated sending, receiving, storage, and retrieval of email messages.

links.text: Receives inbound email from external and internal senders via the Secure Email Platform.
Sends outbound email through the Secure Email Platform with authenticated identity.
Persists messages and metadata subject to records and retention policy.
Generates authentication, access, and mailbox events for centralized audit and investigation.

roles.title: Mailbox Owner
roles.remarks: The individual user accountable for appropriate use of their mailbox under institutional policy.

roles.title: Email Platform Operations
roles.remarks: Operates email infrastructure, identity enforcement, monitoring, and recovery.

roles.title: Email Security Monitoring
roles.remarks: Monitors mailbox activity, phishing indicators, and security events.

roles.title: Records and Compliance Authority
roles.remarks: Defines retention obligations, legal holds, and evidentiary requirements for email communications.

control-implementation.remarks: All security and privacy controls applicable to individual email mailboxes are satisfied through inherited Secure Email Platform implementations and associated patterns. This SSPP introduces no independent controls.
